html:
La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná was a Jesuit mission town in southern Paraguay, founded in 1706. Its great stone church, built in the mid-1700s, is now the best-preserved ruin of the Guarani missions.

It was among the last of the Jesuit reductions, towns where Jesuit priests gathered thousands of Guarani to farm, build and worship, safe from slave raiders and settlers. Guarani carvers decorated the church with a frieze of angels playing musical instruments.

In 1767 Spain expelled the Jesuits, and the towns soon declined. Trinidad and its neighbour, Jesús de Tavarangue, became World Heritage Sites in 1993. They show the mix of European and Guarani skill that made the missions famous across the Paraguay region, and the Guarani that the missions helped keep alive.
